messages.content: What parameters do the viscous friction force depend on, and in which case should it be taken into account for the physical pendulum model? In your response the last word of each sentence must become the first word of the next sentence.

message.content: Viscous friction depends on velocity. Velocity determines the damping coefficient. The coefficient is often denoted as $b$. This force opposes motion direction. Direction matters for energy loss. Loss occurs over time intervals. Intervals require experimental measurement. Measurement yields specific values. Values define the system response. Response includes amplitude decay. Decay affects oscillation frequency. Frequency shifts slightly under damping. Damping must be included in models. Models assume small angles. Angles allow linear approximation. Approximation simplifies differential equations. Equations describe pendulum dynamics. Dynamics reveal stability limits. Limits determine valid conditions. Conditions justify neglecting air resistance. Resistance is negligible at low speeds. Speeds remain below critical thresholds.
